title: Federal Law: H.R.1 One Big Beautiful Bill Act (P.L. 119-21) - Medicaid Provisions

sections.title: Requirement for States to Establish Medicaid Community Engagement Requirements
sections.summary: Requires states to condition Medicaid eligibility for applicable individuals (ACA expansion adults 19-64) on completing 80 hours/month of qualifying activities or meeting income threshold. Must be implemented no later than first quarter after Dec 31, 2026 (i.e., Jan 1, 2027), at state option earlier. Optional good-faith delay to Dec 31, 2028 at Secretary discretion.

sections.title: What Counts as Community Engagement
sections.summary: Individual meets requirement if in the month they: (A) work >=80 hrs; (B) complete >=80 hrs community service; (C) participate in work program >=80 hrs; (D) enrolled at least half-time in educational program; (E) any combination totaling >=80 hrs; (F) have monthly income >= federal minimum wage x 80 hrs ($580 at $7.25); (G) seasonal/irregular income: average monthly income over prior 6 months >= $580.

sections.title: Who Is Subject
sections.summary: Applies to nonpregnant, nondisabled adults aged 19-64 eligible for Medicaid under ACA expansion group (1902(a)(10)(A)(i)(VIII)) or Section 1115 waiver providing minimum essential coverage. Excludes children, seniors 65+, pregnant/postpartum, aged/blind/disabled, those entitled to Medicare. 40 states and DC have adopted the ACA expansion; 10 states have not. The requirement applies to the states and DC that have it (expansion/waiver MEC population). U.S. territories not subject. (Corrected per CRS R48633; cf. prior '43 jurisdictions' phrasing.)

sections.title: Excluded Individuals (No Work Requirement)
sections.summary: Must be exempted: parents/guardians/caretaker relatives/family caregivers of dependent child age 13 or under OR disabled individual; veterans with total disability rating; medically frail or special medical needs; those complying with TANF work requirements; SNAP recipients not exempt from SNAP work; inmates; those in last 90 days after release; pregnant/postpartum 12mo; American Indians/Alaska Natives; certain former foster youth; those entitled/enrolled in Medicare Part A or B.

sections.title: CMS Interim Final Rule (IFR)
sections.summary: CMS issued IFC June 1, 2026, published June 3, 2026 (91 FR 33348), effective July 31, 2026. Verification: at application (look-back 1-3 consecutive months prior) and between redeterminations (>=1 month). Must use ex parte data matching BEFORE asking enrollee. 30-day cure period after notice of noncompliance.
